points: Something outside your control (a ball, a person, a pet) that really gets in your way gives a let. The whole point is replayed, so the server gets two serves.
Any player on the court may call that let, as soon as they notice. You cannot play on and claim it after you miss.
Something within your control is never a let: your own hat, your own dropped ball, your own phone.
Your opponent distracts you on purpose: call a hindrance and you win the point. By accident: call a let and replay the point.
Moving and feinting with your body is legal. Waving arms or racket, stamping feet or making noise to distract is not.
Singles: do not talk during points. Doubles: talk to your partner only while the ball is coming toward you.
An injury gives a 3 minute medical timeout. After it you play on or retire. There is no extra time for cramps or tiredness.

questions.q: During a rally, a ball from the next court rolls behind you and puts you off. What can you do?
options: Call a let at once. The whole point is replayed
Play on, and claim a let if you lose the point
Nothing. Only your opponent can call that let
Claim the point
questions.why: Something outside your control that really gets in your way gives a let, and the whole point is replayed. Claim it at once.

questions.q: A ball rolls onto your court during a rally. Who may call the let?
options: Any player on that court
Only the player closest to the ball
Only the team on that side of the net
Only the server
questions.why: Any player on the court may call a let as soon as they notice the ball or other interference.

questions.q: The first serve was a fault. During the rally after the second serve, a let is called for a ball rolling on. How many serves does the server get?
options: Two serves
One serve
One serve, unless the receiver offers two
The server loses the point
questions.why: A let replays the whole point, even if the first serve was already a fault. The server gets two serves again.

questions.q: You see a ball roll onto your court, keep playing, and miss your shot. Then you ask for a let. Do you get it?
options: No. You had to claim it at once
Yes. The ball was on the court
Yes, if your opponent saw the ball too
Yes, but only once per set
questions.why: Claim a let at once. You cannot play on and claim it after you miss.

questions.q: Your own hat falls off in the middle of a point and puts you off. Can you call a let?
options: No. Play on or lose the point
Yes, the first time it happens
Yes, if it landed in the court
Yes, if you stop right away
questions.why: Something within your control is never a let. Your own hat, your own dropped ball, your own phone: no let.

questions.q: As you hit an overhead, your opponent waves their arms and shouts to put you off. You stop and claim it. What is the call?
options: Hindrance on purpose. You win the point
A let. Replay the point
No call. Anything goes during a point
A warning the first time
questions.why: Waving arms or making noise to distract is a hindrance. When it is on purpose, you call it and win the point.

questions.q: Your opponent gets stung by a bee and cries out just as you hit. What can you do?
options: Claim a let. The point is replayed
Claim the point
Nothing. Shouts of pain do not count
Wait and see if your shot goes in, then decide
questions.why: A shout of pain or surprise is not on purpose, so the other side may claim a let and the point is replayed.

questions.q: While you toss the ball to serve, the receiver's partner moves from the net back to the baseline. Is that allowed?
options: Yes. Moving and feinting with the body is legal
No. Nobody may move during the toss
No. It is a hindrance and you win the point
Only if they told you first
questions.why: Feinting with your body and moving position is legal at any time, also while the server is tossing.

questions.q: In doubles, when is it fine to talk to your partner during a point?
options: While the ball is coming toward your side
While the ball is going toward the opponents
At any time, if you keep it short
Never during a point
questions.why: Talking to your partner is fine while the ball travels toward you. It is not fine while the ball travels toward your opponents.

questions.q: Doubles. You hit a weak lob and yell 'back!' to your partner. Your opponent stops at once and claims a hindrance. What is the call?
options: They win the point
Replay the point
No call. You may always talk to your partner
You win the point because they stopped
questions.why: You talked while the ball was travelling toward your opponents. If they stop at once and claim it, they win the point.

questions.q: Same lob, same yell of 'back!'. This time your opponent hits the overhead, misses it, and then claims a hindrance. What is the call?
options: They lose the point. They claimed it too late
They win the point. The yell was a hindrance
Replay the point
Replay it, with a warning for you
questions.why: A hindrance must be claimed at once. If they play the overhead and miss, they lose the point.

questions.q: In singles, what is the rule about talking during a point?
options: Do not talk. Talk that gets in the opponent's way is a hindrance
Talking is fine while the ball is on your side
Talking is fine if it is to yourself
Talking is fine until someone complains
questions.why: Singles: do not talk during points. Any talking that interferes with your opponent playing the ball is a hindrance.

questions.q: You twist your ankle during the match. How long is the medical timeout?
options: 2 minutes
3 minutes
5 minutes
10 minutes
questions.why: In case of injury you can have a 3 minute medical timeout. After it you either play on or retire.

questions.q: Late in the second set you are worn out and cramping. Can you take extra time to recover?
options: No. There is no extra time just to recover
Yes, one break of 3 minutes
Yes, if the opponent agrees to 5 minutes
Yes, at the next changeover only
questions.why: No extra time is available simply to recover condition: cramps, exhaustion or catching your breath.

questions.q: After the medical timeout you cannot go on, and you retire. What is the result?
options: Your opponent is awarded the match
The match is recorded as a tie
The match is replayed on another day
The score stands as it was when you stopped
questions.why: If you retire, the opponent is awarded the match.
